newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's MRCB signs pact with Pidemco.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's MRCB signs pact with Pidemco.

text.p: Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd (MRCB) signed on Tuesday a 200 million ringgit ($80 million) joint venture agreement with Singapore's Pidemco Land Ltd to build condominiums in Kuala Lumpur.
The two companies agreed to build two blocks of 400-unit condominiums in the Kuala Lumpur Sentral project, MRCB said in a statement.
MRCB will hold 51 percent of the shares in the joint venture and Pidemco 49 percent, with project construction to begin early next year and due to be completed within three years.
Kuala Lumpur Sentral is a 72-acre (29 ha) parcel located in the main railway yard of Malaysian state railway company which is being converted into a mini-city.
MRCB holds a 64 percent stake in the 3-4 billion ringgit development, which includes hotels, office buildings, condos, a sports centre and express railway links to the new Kuala Lumpur airport.
MRCB executive chairman Khalid Ahmad, noting that Pidemco is a unit of Singapore Technologies and MRCB has a multimedia division, said the two companies were exploring other synergies.

The development's managing director Wong Dor Loke told reporters after the signing ceremony that Singaporeans are one of the main target markets for the condominiums, despite a 100,000 ringgit surcharge on foreign purchases of Malaysian property.

Pidemco is the third foreign investor involved in Kuala Lumpur Sentral. MRCB last week signed deals with Daito Trust Construction Co to develop a four-star hotel and another with an unnamed Japanese investor to develop a five-star hotel.
Two other condominium blocks are planned in the development. Wong said MRCB is talking with both local and foreign investors about joint ventures for their construction.
